question: Which mineral fuel product chapters (HS4) showed the largest changes in import value between 2021 and 2022 in Luxembourg?

limitations.message: Values are in current euros (nominal), not adjusted for price changes.
37.8 % of this value is confidential at full product detail (masked codes); it is shown as a separate 'Confidential' slice, never dropped.

sql:
SELECT
  year,
  hs4 AS key,
  flow,
  SUM(value_eur) AS value_eur,
  SUM(qty_kg) AS qty_kg,
  SUM(value_eur) FILTER(WHERE
    NOT qty_kg IS NULL) AS value_eur_with_qty
FROM v_lu_trade
WHERE
  period >= CAST('2021-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND period < CAST('2023-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND flow = 'import'
  AND hs2 IN ('27')
  AND year IN (2021, 2022)
GROUP BY
  year,
  key,
  flow
ORDER BY
  year,
  value_eur DESC
LIMIT 10000
title: Largest changes by product group — imports 2021–2022

main.label: Coal; briquettes, ovoids and similar solid fuels manufactured from coal
Bituminous mastics, cut-backs and other bituminous mixtures based on natural asphalt, on natural bitumen, on petroleum bitumen, on mineral tar or on mineral tar pitch

Petroleum jelly, paraffin wax, micro- crystalline petroleum wax, slack wax, ozokerite, lignite wax, peat wax, other mineral waxes, and similar products obtained by synthesis or by other processes, whether or not coloured
Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, crude
Peat, incl. peat litter, whether or not agglomerated
Tar distilled from coal, from lignite or from peat, and other mineral tars, whether or not dehydrated or partially distilled, incl. reconstituted tars
Bitumen and asphalt, natural; bituminous or oil-shale and tar sands; asphaltites and asphaltic rocks

insight: The mineral fuel product chapters that showed the largest changes in import value between 2021 and 2022 in Luxembourg were Petroleum oils and Coal; briquettes, ovoids and similar solid fuels manufactured from coal.
Imports of Petroleum oils increased by 1.09 billion euros, reaching 2.39 billion euros in 2022, while imports of Coal rose by 6.8 million euros to 11.0 million euros.
The largest percentage increase was in Coal imports, which grew by 162.7%.
Imports of Petroleum jelly and related products nearly doubled, increasing by 2.3 million euros to 4.6 million euros in 2022.
The data are limited because 37.8% of the import values at full product detail are confidential and values are nominal, not adjusted for price changes.
